judge: context_ok is False — Verified by hand. g002: 3200 x 1.05^2 = 3200 x 1.1025 = 3528. g004: 48000 x 1.25^3 = 48000 x 1.953125 = 93750. g008: 16000 x 1.953125 = 31250. Step 4 jumps straight to the result with no intermediate value, which is thin but not wrong.

context_ok is false because of realism. g004 and g008 give a town an average population growth of 25% p.a. A town that grows by a quarter every year, nearly doubling in 3 years (48000 to 93750), is not a plausible reading of 'average rate of population growth'. Real growth rates are a few percent. The 25% looks picked only because 1.25^3 = 125/64 gives an integer result. g004 also calls a town of 48000 'small'. g002 (5%, 3200, 2 years) is realistic and matches the book's original. The maths is fine and nothing is ambiguous. Fix: swap the 25% instances for realistic rates (about 2% to 8%) with populations that give whole-number answers, for example 6250 at 4% for 2 years gives 6760, or 8000 at 5% for 3 years gives 9261. Keep the 'small town' populations in the low thousands to tens of thousands. A rejected family costs a rewrite, but 25% town growth would teach a Grade 10 student an unrealistic picture of the context.

questions.stem: Adam opens a savings account when he is $13$ years old. He would like to have $\text{R87000}$ by the time he is $18$ years old. If the savings account offers simple interest at a rate of $8.5$ % per annum, how much money should he invest now to reach his goal? Give your answer in rand, correct to two decimal places.

canonical_solution.text_md: Work out how many years the money is invested: $n=18-13=5$ years.
Write down the given information: $\begin{aligned}A&=\text{R87000}\\P&=?\\i&=\frac{8.5}{100}=0.085\\n&=5\end{aligned}$
Write down the simple interest formula: $A=P(1+in)$
Substitute the given values and work out the bracket: $\begin{aligned}\text{R87000}&=P\left(1+0.085\times5\right)\\\text{R87000}&=P\times1.425\end{aligned}$
Divide both sides by $1.425$ to find $P$: $P=\frac{\text{R87000}}{1.425}$
Calculate and round to two decimal places: $P=\text{R61052.63}$
Adam should invest $\text{R61052.63}$ now.

How much more money does Bianca have in the account at Bank B than in the account at Bank A at the end of the 2 years? Give your answer in rand.

canonical_solution.text_md: Bank A pays simple interest, so use $A=P(1+in)$ with $P=800$, $i=0.20$ and $n=2$.
$\begin{aligned}A&=800(1+(0.20)(2))\\A&=\text{R 1120}\end{aligned}$
Bank B pays compound interest, so use $A=P(1+i)^{n}$ with $P=800$, $i=0.20$ and $n=2$.
The difference between the two closing balances is $\text{R 1152}-\text{R 1120}=\text{R 32}$.
Bianca has $\text{R 32}$ more in the compound interest account at Bank B, because in the second year it also earns interest on the first year's interest.

questions.stem: Thandi buys a fridge on hire purchase. The cash price of the fridge is $\text{R9000}$. The agreement runs for $5 \times 12 = 60$ months, so the monthly repayment on the hire purchase agreement is $\frac{13050.00}{60} = \text{R217.50}$ (to the nearest cent).
Add the insurance premium to the monthly repayment: $\text{R217.50} + \text{R12.80} = \text{R230.30}$.
Thandi's monthly payment is $\text{R230.30}$.
